body: Three defects worth naming. First, the central physics here is trivial and the spec never confronts it: with independent noise per objective and normalized weights w_i summing to 1, the variance of the weighted advantage is Σw_i²σ_i², which is at most σ² and decreases toward σ²/N — it does NOT grow 'super-linearly' with N as the motivating idea claims. The super-linear claim holds only for unnormalized sums, and which convention is used changes the entire scaling law, the lower bound, and every TOST margin downstream. FR-001 demands 'a closed-form mathematical equation' but never pins down the weight normalization, so the 'theoretical slope' that FR-006/SC-007 test against is undefined until this is fixed. Second, the statistical machinery is internally inconsistent: SC-004 tests a false-positive rate ≤ 0.10 against 'a null hypothesis of 0.5' — a coin-flip null is not the right comparator for a stability criterion, and the ±0.1 TOST margin on a slope coefficient is scale-dependent (a slope of 0.1 in what units — samples per objective? log-samples?). Third, mechanical issues: FR-008 and FR-011 are missing from the numbering; FR-019 and User Story 2 contain unresolved '[deferred]' placeholders in the definition of the convergence metric, so SC-002's 5% failure threshold and the convergence-speed logging are unmeasurable as written; and FR-016's remedy — halving the state space when N > 50 — has no stated connection between state-space size and objective count (N reward functions do not inflate a tabular state space), so the guard addresses a coupling the spec never establishes.
